extracted.intended_audience: Users of the PARI/GP library (mathematicians, computational number theorists, and developers calling GEN functions)
extracted.subtask_description: Reference documentation for PARI/GP library functions: descriptions, parameter semantics, algorithmic notes, flags, warnings, and examples for a broad set of number-theoretic and algebraic routines.

rubrics_metrics.name: factorint (integer factorization engine)
rubrics_metrics.description: Provides direct access to the integer factoring engine called by most arithmetical functions. Optional binary-encoded flag controls which algorithms to avoid or skip: 1 avoid MPQS, 2 skip first-stage ECM, 4 avoid Rho and SQUFOF, 8 don't run final ECM (which may cause a huge composite to be declared prime). Uses a (strong) probabilistic primality test; composites might not be detected though no example is known.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: You may set factor_proven default to 1 or run isprime on results to guarantee primality. Use gp’s debug parameter to inspect internals (level 3+). Note risks when disabling ECM/fallbacks; probabilistic nature implies rare false primes; monitor debug to see warnings about untested cofactors.

rubrics_metrics.name: factormod (factor polynomial mod p)
rubrics_metrics.description: Factors polynomial x modulo prime p using Berlekamp; coefficients of x must be operation-compatible with Z/pZ. Returns two-column matrix: irreducible polynomials and their exponents. If flag non-zero, outputs only degrees of irreducibles.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A different algorithm factorcantor may be faster in some cases. Ensure coefficient types are compatible; examples show usage for finite-field factorization and option to return degrees (useful for e.g. L-functions).

rubrics_metrics.name: ffgen (finite field generator)
rubrics_metrics.description: Return a t_FFELT generator for finite field with q elements (q = p^f). Computes an irreducible monic polynomial P ∈ Fp[X] of degree f via ffinit and returns g = X (mod P(X)). If v provided, use its variable name for display.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Alternative inputs: pair [p,f] or directly the polynomial P (must be monic irreducible with t_INTMOD coefficients). If P is not irreducible, an invalid object is created and behavior is undefined — testing irreducibility is costlier than producing P via ffinit. Errors shown if q is not a prime power. Use ffgen(ffinit(...)) idiom to combine init and generator creation.

rubrics_metrics.name: ffinit (compute monic irreducible polynomial)
rubrics_metrics.description: Computes a monic irreducible polynomial of degree n over Fp (p prime) using a fast variant of Adleman–Lenstra’s algorithm.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Useful with ffgen to represent elements of F_{p^n}. Example: P=ffinit(3,2) then ffgen(P,'t'). Library syntax includes variable selection. Assumes input p is prime (no primality test performed).

rubrics_metrics.name: fflog (discrete logarithm in finite field)
rubrics_metrics.description: Discrete logarithm of finite-field element x in base g: returns e in Z such that g^e = x. Optional parameter o represents multiplicative order of g (preferred format [ord, factor(ord)]). If o omitted, g assumed primitive root. Result undefined if logarithm does not exist.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Algorithms used vary by field: generic discrete-log (via znlog), cubic-sieve index-calculus for large fields deg≥5, Coppersmith’s algorithm for small characteristic ≤5. Providing o (order and factorisation) speeds/assists computation; can be obtained by ffprimroot. Examples demonstrate computing o and fflog with/without o.

rubrics_metrics.name: ffnbirred (number of monic irreducible polynomials)
rubrics_metrics.description: Computes number of monic irreducible polynomials over F_q of degree exactly n (flag=0) or at most n (flag=1).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Multiple wrappers available (ffnbirred, ffsumnbirred). Ensure q is a prime power input in accepted formats.

rubrics_metrics.name: fforder (multiplicative order in finite field)
rubrics_metrics.description: Multiplicative order of t_FFELT element x. Optional o may be provided as a multiple of the order in format [N, factor(N)] where N is group cardinality.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Providing o accelerates or avoids recomputation; examples show timing difference when o provided. Use ffprimroot to obtain o for generator elements.

rubrics_metrics.name: ffprimroot (primitive root of multiplicative group)
rubrics_metrics.description: Return a primitive root of the multiplicative group of the definition field of finite-field element x. Optional output o set to [ord, fa] where ord is group order and fa its factorization.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: o is useful for fflog and fforder. Note returned primitive root may not lie in field generated by x. Example shows computing o and using it to compute discrete logs quickly.

rubrics_metrics.name: fibonacci (fibo)
rubrics_metrics.description: fibonacci(x) returns the x-th Fibonacci number.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Library syntax is GEN fibo(long x). Straightforward; used for integer-indexed Fibonacci values.

rubrics_metrics.name: gcd (greatest common divisor)
rubrics_metrics.description: Creates gcd(x,y). If y omitted and x is vector, returns gcd of components (equiv. to content(x)). For vector/matrix inputs, gcd applied recursively with semantics depending on which argument is vector/matrix; gcd is not commutative for these types.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Algorithms: naive Euclid generally, but special cases: integers use modified right-shift binary algorithm; univariate polynomials over same number field use modular gcd; general polynomials use subresultant when coefficient explosion likely. For inexact polynomial coefficients gcd is scalar; use polresultant to check near-degeneracy, or gcdext to compute approximate gcd and cofactors. Multiple wrappers exist: ggcd0, ggcd, content.

rubrics_metrics.name: gcdext (extended gcd)
rubrics_metrics.description: Returns [u, v, d] with d = gcd(x,y) and x*u + y*v = d; u and v minimal. Arguments must be integers or polynomials. For inexact polynomial coefficients it computes u,v,d with approximate division properties rather than the scalar gcd.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples show integer and polynomial outputs. For inexact inputs outputs are not mathematically well-defined but give explicit polynomials to check approximation quality. Library wrapper gcdext0.

rubrics_metrics.name: hilbert (Hilbert symbol)
rubrics_metrics.description: Hilbert symbol of x and y modulo prime p; p=0 denotes the infinite place. Result undefined if p≠0 is not prime.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: p may be omitted: take p=0 if both x,y rational or one real; take p=q if one argument is t_INTMOD modulo q or a q-adic. Incompatible types raise an error. Syntax long hilbert(GEN x, GEN y, GEN p = NULL).

rubrics_metrics.name: isfundamental (fundamental discriminant check)
rubrics_metrics.description: True (1) if x equals 1 or the discriminant of a quadratic field, false (0) otherwise.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Simple predicate; library syntax long isfundamental(GEN x).

rubrics_metrics.name: ispolygonal (s-gonal number test)
rubrics_metrics.description: ispolygonal(x,s,{&N}) returns true if integer x is s-gonal (s>2 t_INT). If &N provided, sets N to index n such that x is n-th s-gonal number.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example shows usage with &N. Ensure s is integer >2 and types correct. Syntax long ispolygonal(GEN x, GEN s, GEN *N = NULL).

rubrics_metrics.name: ispower (k-th power detection/maximal power)
rubrics_metrics.description: If k given, returns true if x is k-th power (meaning depends on x type). If k omitted, for integer/fraction x returns maximal k≥2 with x = n^k else 0. If &n provided and x is k-th power set n to k-th root.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For t_FFELT x omitting k not allowed; one may set k = (x.p^x.f - 1)/fforder(x). Also gisanypower exists to return type information. Library syntax long ispower(GEN x, GEN k = NULL, GEN *n = NULL).

rubrics_metrics.name: ispowerful (powerful integer test)
rubrics_metrics.description: True if integer x is powerful (valuation at all primes dividing x ≥ 2), false otherwise.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples show 50 -> 0, 100 -> 1, support for huge expressions. Library syntax long ispowerful(GEN x).

rubrics_metrics.name: isprime (primality test and proven certificates)
rubrics_metrics.description: True (1) if x is prime, false (0) otherwise. This routine proves/disproves rigorously (slow for large primes > ~1000 digits). For quick compositeness check use ispseudoprime. Accepts vectors/matrices componentwise.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: flag=0: uses Baillie-PSW, Selfridge p-1 if x-1 smooth enough, and APRCL for general x. flag=1: use Selfridge-Pocklington-Lehmer p-1 test and output a primality certificate: returns 0 composite, 1 if small enough that Baillie-PSW suffices (currently x<2^64), 2 if large prime provable only by APRCL, or a three-column matrix certificate when x-1 is smooth enough. Algorithm may fail extremely rarely if pseudo-prime factors are composite — monitor debug warnings about untested cofactors. flag=2: use APRCL. Use isprime to get rigorously proven primes; otherwise probabilistic pseudoprimality tests may be faster.

rubrics_metrics.name: isprimepower (prime power detection)
rubrics_metrics.description: If x = p^k with p prime and k>0, return k else 0. If &n given and true, sets n to p.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Syntax long isprimepower(GEN x, GEN *n = NULL). Straightforward predicate for prime-power structure.

rubrics_metrics.name: ispseudoprime (strong pseudoprime testing)
rubrics_metrics.description: Returns true if x is a strong pseudoprime by specified test, false otherwise. If false then x is composite; if true x is only highly likely prime. Accepts vectors/matrices componentwise.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: flag=0: check small prime divisors up to 101 and Baillie-Pomerance-Selfridge-Wagstaff pseudo-prime (Rabin-Miller base 2 followed by Lucas test for sequence (P,-1)). No known composites pass this test; all composites ≤ 2^64 are correctly detected. flag>0: strong Miller-Rabin pseudo prime for flag randomly-chosen bases (with end-matching for sqrt(-1) detection). Use isprime for rigorous proof.

rubrics_metrics.name: ispseudoprimepower (pseudo-prime power detection)
rubrics_metrics.description: If x = p^k with p a pseudoprime (per ispseudoprime) and k>0, return k else 0. If &n given and true, sets n to p.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: k is maximal such that x = n^k, and when n ≤ 2^64 the function returns k>0 iff n is truly prime; for n > 2^64 a pseudoprime test is used so composite factors may be mistaken for prime.

rubrics_metrics.name: issquare (square detection and root)
rubrics_metrics.description: True if x is a square, false otherwise. Meaning of square depends on type: all complex numbers are squares; nonnegative real are squares; exact types t_INT,t_FRAC,t_INTMOD squares as per their domains. If &n given, sets n to a square root.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Polynomials: detect characteristic 2 or assume 2 invertible and verify by squaring truncated power series. For t_POLMOD only support t_POLMODs of t_INTMODs encoding finite fields (assume without checking that modulus p is prime and polynomial irreducible). Deprecated GP wrappers exist. Syntax long issquareall(GEN x, GEN *n = NULL). Examples show different contexts (integer, real, mod, p-adic).

rubrics_metrics.name: issquarefree (squarefree test)
rubrics_metrics.description: True if x is squarefree, false otherwise. x may be integer or polynomial with coefficients in an integral domain. A polynomial is declared squarefree if gcd(x, x') = 1. Non-zero polynomials with inexact coefficients are considered squarefree.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Note possible inconsistency with factor which rounds input to an exact approximation before factoring; use polresultant to check closeness to inseparability. Errors shown when domain invalid (e.g., Z/4Z). Syntax long issquarefree(GEN x).

rubrics_metrics.name: istotient (totient value test)
rubrics_metrics.description: Returns true if x = φ(n) for some integer n, false otherwise. If &N provided, set N = n as well.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: istotient(4,&n) gives n=10. Syntax long istotient(GEN x, GEN *N = NULL).

rubrics_metrics.name: kronecker (Kronecker symbol)
rubrics_metrics.description: Kronecker symbol (x|y) for integer arguments, extension of Legendre symbol by multiplicativity with special rules for y=0,-1,2: (x|0)=1 if |x|=1 else 0; (x|-1)=1 if x≥0 else -1; (x|2)=0 if x even, 1 if x≡1 or -1 mod 8, -1 if x≡3 or -3 mod 8.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Input types must be integer. Syntax long kronecker(GEN x, GEN y). Use for quadratic character computations.

rubrics_metrics.name: lcm (least common multiple)
rubrics_metrics.description: Least common multiple of x and y such that lcm(x,y)*gcd(x,y) = x*y up to units. If y omitted and x is a vector, returns lcm of components (a scalar). For vector/matrix arguments recursion rules produce result type matching vector/matrix argument; lcm is not commutative for these types.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Note lcm(v) differs from iterative lcm accumulation l = v[1]; for(i,..) l=lcm(l,v[i]) — former returns scalar and uses divide-and-conquer tree for efficiency, especially with GMP kernel. Example demonstrates performance difference on large vectors. Syntax GEN glcm0(GEN x, GEN y = NULL).

rubrics_metrics.name: logint (integer logarithm floor)
rubrics_metrics.description: Return largest integer e such that b^e ≤ x for integers b>1 and x>0. If z provided set it to b^e. May replace floor(log(x)/log(b)) which can be incorrect due to rounding.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Useful to compute digit counts: #digits(1000!,10)=1+logint(1000!,10). Syntax long logint0(GEN x, GEN b, GEN *z = NULL).

rubrics_metrics.name: moebius (Moebius μ function)
rubrics_metrics.description: Compute Moebius µ(|x|) where x must be integer.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Simple arithmetic function; syntax long moebius(GEN x).

rubrics_metrics.name: nextprime (next pseudoprime ≥ x)
rubrics_metrics.description: Finds smallest pseudoprime (per ispseudoprime) greater than or equal to x. If x itself is pseudoprime it is returned. To rigorously prove primality, use isprime.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Accepts real-type x. Returned value may be pseudoprime; call isprime if a proven prime is required. Syntax GEN nextprime(GEN x).

rubrics_metrics.name: numbpart (number of unrestricted partitions p(n))
rubrics_metrics.description: Gives number p(n) of unrestricted partitions of integer n (n<10^15); algorithm uses Hardy–Ramanujan–Rademacher formula. Trivial values p(n)=0 for n<0 and p(0)=1.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If explicit enumeration needed use partitions. Syntax GEN numbpart(GEN n).

rubrics_metrics.name: numdiv (number of divisors)
rubrics_metrics.description: Number of divisors of |x| for integer x.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Simple arithmetic function; syntax GEN numdiv(GEN x).

rubrics_metrics.name: omega and bigomega (count prime divisors)
rubrics_metrics.description: omega(x) = number of distinct prime divisors of |x|. bigomega (implied) = number of prime divisors counted with multiplicity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example factor(392) leads to omega(392)=2 and bigomega=5. Syntax long omega(GEN x).

rubrics_metrics.name: partitions (list partitions with bounds)
rubrics_metrics.description: Returns vector of partitions of integer k as sums of positive integers; optional parameters a (part bounds) and n (length bounds) allow restricting parts and lengths. By default zero entries removed unless amin ≤ 0 then fixed-length vectors returned.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Parts are Vecsmall sorted nondecreasingly. Examples show limiting parts ≤2, at most 2 parts, etc. Use numbpart to get counts. Syntax GEN partitions(long k, GEN a = NULL, GEN n = NULL).

rubrics_metrics.name: polrootsff (roots in finite field defined by poly)
rubrics_metrics.description: Returns vector of distinct roots of polynomial x in field F_q defined by irreducible polynomial a over F_p. Coefficients of x must be operation-compatible with Z/pZ. Either a or p may be omitted if x has t_FFELT coefficients.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If insufficient information to determine base field an error occurs. Better syntax uses ffgen for readability. t_FFELT coefficients avoid specifying p,a explicitly. Syntax GEN polrootsff(GEN x, GEN p = NULL, GEN a = NULL).

rubrics_metrics.name: precprime (previous pseudoprime ≤ x)
rubrics_metrics.description: Find largest pseudoprime ≤ x; returns 0 if x ≤ 1. If x is a prime it is returned; use isprime for rigorous proof.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Accepts real-type x. As with nextprime, returned value may be pseudoprime — call isprime if needed. Syntax GEN precprime(GEN x).

rubrics_metrics.name: prime (nth prime)
rubrics_metrics.description: prime(n) returns nth prime number. Uses checkpointing and naive O(n) algorithm.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example prime(10^9) yields large prime. Not optimized for huge n. Syntax GEN prime(long n).

rubrics_metrics.name: primepi (prime counting function)
rubrics_metrics.description: primepi(x) returns number of primes p ≤ x. Implementation uses checkpointing and naive O(x) algorithm.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples show large values; expect slow behavior for very large x due to naive algorithm. Syntax GEN primepi(GEN x).

rubrics_metrics.name: primes (list primes or primes in interval)
rubrics_metrics.description: Creates row vector of first n primes, or if input is vector [a,b] returns primes in [a,b].
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Returns empty vector for n ≤ 0. Examples show primes(10) and primes([a,b]). Syntax GEN primes0(GEN n).

rubrics_metrics.name: qfbclassno (ordinary class number of quadratic order)
rubrics_metrics.description: Compute class number of quadratic order discriminant D for 'small' D. If D>0 or flag=1 use O(|D|^{1/2}) algorithm (approx functional equation). If D<0 and flag=0 use O(|D|^{1/4}) Shanks baby-step/giant-step method. Function gives unconditionally correct results for |D|<2e10 in Shanks mode but may be incorrect for larger D if class group has many cyclic factors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recommendation: double-check results for larger D using quadclassunit, which is 2–3x slower but more robust (assumes GRH for provable correctness in some regimes). Warning about naming: qfbclassno does not compute number of classes of primitive forms (narrow class number) in all cases; use QFBclassno(D) = qfbclassno(D) * if(D<0||norm(quadunit(D))<0,1,2) to correct in some situations. Syntax GEN qfbclassno0(GEN D, long flag) and wrapper functions classno/classno2 exist. Use hclassno for imaginary quadratic fields via O(|D|) algorithm.

rubrics_metrics.name: qfbcompraw (composition of binary quadratic forms without reduction)
rubrics_metrics.description: Composition of binary quadratic forms x and y without reducing the result. Useful to compute generating element of an ideal. Result undefined if discriminants differ.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Raw composition may be needed prior to reduction. Syntax GEN qfbcompraw(GEN x, GEN y).

rubrics_metrics.name: qfbhclassno (Hurwitz class number)
rubrics_metrics.description: Hurwitz class number of x for x≥0, x≡0 or 3 mod 4. For x>5e5 assume GRH and use quadclassunit with default parameters.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Syntax GEN hclassno(GEN x). Note GRH assumption for large x.

rubrics_metrics.name: qfbnucomp (NUCOMP composition for primitive positive definite forms)
rubrics_metrics.description: Composition of primitive positive definite binary quadratic forms x and y (type t_QFI) using NUCOMP/NUDUPL algorithms; requires L parameter (optimal L≈|D/4|^{1/4}). Result undefined if discriminants differ.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Implementation slower than generic routine for small D and becomes faster near D with about 45 bits. Use nudupl when x=y. Syntax GEN nucomp(GEN x, GEN y, GEN L).

rubrics_metrics.name: qfbnupow (n-th power using NUCOMP/NUDUPL)
rubrics_metrics.description: n-th power of primitive positive definite binary quadratic form x using NUCOMP/NUDUPL; optional L should equal sqrt_nint(abs(D)>>2,4).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Faster for large discriminant; slower than generic for small D; becomes faster for D≈2^45. Syntax GEN nupow(GEN x, GEN n, GEN L = NULL).

rubrics_metrics.name: qfbpowraw (n-th raw power without reduction)
rubrics_metrics.description: Compute n-th power of binary quadratic form x without reduction, using qfbcompraw. Here n must be non-negative and <2^31.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use when reduction is not desired or will be handled separately. Syntax GEN qfbpowraw(GEN x, long n).

rubrics_metrics.name: qfbprimeform (prime binary quadratic form)
rubrics_metrics.description: Prime binary quadratic form of discriminant x whose first coefficient is p (|p| prime). p=±1 returns unit form. Error if x not quadratic residue mod p or x<0 and p<0. Negative definite t_QFI not implemented. For x>0 distance component set to zero according to current precision.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Syntax GEN primeform(GEN x, GEN p, long prec). Check residue conditions before calling.

rubrics_metrics.name: qfbred (reduce binary quadratic form)
rubrics_metrics.description: Reduce binary quadratic form x; optional flag binary digits: 1 perform single reduction step, 2 don't update Shanks's distance. Optional arguments supply discriminant and square-root values (no checking). For d<0 Shanks distance irrelevant.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Multiple wrappers available for de/indefinite, real/imag reductions: redimag, redreal, rhoreal, redrealnod, rhorealnod. Provide precomputed discriminant/sqrt to avoid recomputation but ensure correctness. Syntax GEN qfbred0(GEN x, long flag, GEN d = NULL, GEN isd = NULL, GEN sd = NULL).

rubrics_metrics.name: qfbredsl2 (reduction with SL(2,Z) transform)
rubrics_metrics.description: Reduce real or imaginary binary quadratic form x and return [y,g] where y reduced and g in SL(2,Z) with g·x = y. Optional data [D, sqrtint(D)] may be supplied. For t_QFR forms distance component unaffected.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Useful when the SL(2,Z) transform is also needed. Syntax GEN qfbredsl2(GEN x, GEN data = NULL).

rubrics_metrics.name: qfbsolve (solve Q(x,y)=p over integers)
rubrics_metrics.description: Solve equation Q(x,y)=p where Q binary quadratic form and p prime. Returns [x,y] as two-component vector or 0 if no solution. Returns only one solution, not all.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Algorithm: probabilistic polynomial time in p (needs sqrt of D mod p); polynomial in D if Q imaginary, exponential if Q real (full cycle of reduced forms). For real case bnfisprincipal may give heuristic subexponential solution assuming GRH. Syntax GEN qfbsolve(GEN Q, GEN p).

rubrics_metrics.name: quadclassunit (Buchmann–McCurley sub-exponential class group algorithm)
rubrics_metrics.description: Compute class group of quadratic order discriminant D (sub-exponential algorithm). Recommended instead of qfbclassno or quadregulator when D < -1e25, D>1e10, or when structure is wanted. Returns vector v with member functions v.no (class number), v.cyc (structure as product of cyclic groups), v.gen (generators), v.reg (regulator) computed to internal accuracy or default precision.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Flag obsolete; tech parameter [c1,c2] can balance relation finding vs linear algebra, but typical use should not change defaults. c1 influences relation ease/linear algebra cost; c2 mostly obsolete and overwritten to provably-correct choice under GRH. Alternatives: Buchquad wrapper for experimenting with tech. Syntax GEN quadclassunit0(GEN D, long flag, GEN tech = NULL, long prec). Use bnfnarrow for narrow class group when needed.

rubrics_metrics.name: quaddisc (discriminant of quadratic étale algebra)
rubrics_metrics.description: Discriminant of étale algebra Q(sqrt(x)): returns 0 for x=0, 1 for x square, otherwise discriminant of quadratic field Q(sqrt(x)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: quaddisc(7)=28, quaddisc(-7)=-7. Syntax GEN quaddisc(GEN x).

rubrics_metrics.name: quadgen (canonical quadratic generator)
rubrics_metrics.description: Create quadratic number ω = (a + sqrt(d))/2 making (1,ω) an integral basis for quadratic order of discriminant D. D must be integer congruent 0 or 1 mod 4 and not a square.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Syntax GEN quadgen(GEN D). Use with quadpoly/quadunit etc.

rubrics_metrics.name: quadhilbert (Hilbert class field equation)
rubrics_metrics.description: Return relative equation defining Hilbert class field of quadratic field of discriminant D. For D<0 uses complex multiplication (Schertz variant); for D>0 uses Stark units and may return vector of extensions whose compositum is requested class field (see bnrstark).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: May return several relative equations in positive D case. Syntax GEN quadhilbert(GEN D, long prec).

rubrics_metrics.name: quadpoly (canonical quadratic polynomial)
rubrics_metrics.description: Creates canonical quadratic polynomial (in variable v) corresponding to discriminant D — minimal polynomial of quadgen(D). D integer ≡0 or 1 mod 4 and not a square.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Optional variable selection; syntax GEN quadpoly0(GEN D, long v = -1).

rubrics_metrics.name: quadray (relative ray class field equation)
rubrics_metrics.description: Relative equation for ray class field of conductor f for quadratic field of discriminant D using analytic methods. Accepts bnf for x^2−D in place of D. For D<0 uses σ function and Schertz method; for D>0 uses Stark’s conjecture and may return vector of relative equations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Uses advanced analytic techniques; see bnrstark for details. Syntax GEN quadray(GEN D, GEN f, long prec).

rubrics_metrics.name: quadregulator (quadratic regulator)
rubrics_metrics.description: Regulator of quadratic field of positive discriminant x. Returns error if x not a discriminant or if x is a square. For large x see quadclassunit.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Syntax GEN quadregulator(GEN x, long prec). Use appropriate precision for regulator computations.

rubrics_metrics.name: quadunit (fundamental unit of real quadratic field)
rubrics_metrics.description: Return fundamental unit of real quadratic field Q(sqrt(D)) where D positive discriminant. If D not fundamental discriminant, probably returns fundamental unit of corresponding order. D must be integer ≡0 or 1 mod 4 and not a square. Result is quadratic number.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Syntax GEN quadunit(GEN D). Use with quadclassunit/quadregulator when needed.

rubrics_metrics.name: ramanujantau (Ramanujan’s tau function at n)
rubrics_metrics.description: Compute τ(n) assuming GRH (to compute class numbers quickly via quadclassunit). Algorithm complexity ~Õ(n^{1/2}) using O(log n) space for individual n. If all values up to N required, use q*eta(q+O(q^N))^24 expansion for Õ(N) time and Õ(N) space.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example shows tauvec vs individual calls: vector approach much faster if many values required. Syntax GEN ramanujantau(GEN n). Note GRH used for speed of class number subroutines.

rubrics_metrics.name: randomprime (generate pseudoprime in interval)
rubrics_metrics.description: Returns a strong pseudoprime in [2,N−1] by default N=2^31. If input is vector [a,b] returns pseudoprime a ≤ p ≤ b; infinite loop if no pseudoprime exists in interval. If upper bound < 2^64 the returned pseudoprime is a proven prime.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Returned value may be only pseudoprime; use isprime to prove primality. Syntax GEN randomprime(GEN N = NULL).

rubrics_metrics.name: removeprimes (remove primes from private prime table)
rubrics_metrics.description: Removes primes listed in x from PARI's private prime table; removeprimes(addprimes()) empties extra prime table. x may be single integer or list. If x omitted list current extra primes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Manage private prime table carefully; syntax GEN removeprimes(GEN x = NULL).

rubrics_metrics.name: sigma / sumdiv (sum of kth powers of divisors)
rubrics_metrics.description: sigma(x,{k=1}) returns sum of k-th powers of positive divisors of |x|. x and k must be integers. sumdiv is alias for k=1.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use for divisor-sum arithmetic functions; syntax GEN sumdivk(GEN x, long k).

rubrics_metrics.name: sqrtint (integer square root)
rubrics_metrics.description: Return integer square root of non-negative integer x (largest y such that y^2 ≤ x).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Useful to avoid floating rounding issues: sqrtint(N) gives exact integer while sqrt(N) may be floating. Syntax GEN sqrtint(GEN x).

rubrics_metrics.name: sqrtnint (integer n-th root)
rubrics_metrics.description: Return integer n-th root of non-negative integer x (largest y with y^n ≤ x). Special case n=2 is sqrtint.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Syntax GEN sqrtnint(GEN x, long n). Use to avoid floating rounding errors when computing integer roots.

rubrics_metrics.name: stirling (Stirling numbers of first/second kind)
rubrics_metrics.description: stirling(n,k,{flag=1}) returns Stirling number of first kind s(n,k) (flag=1) or second kind S(n,k) (flag=2), for non-negative integers n,k. s(n,k) = (−1)^{n−k} times number of permutations with k cycles; S(n,k) number of ways partitioning n elements into k non-empty subsets.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If many s(n,k) needed it's faster to compute polynomial x(x−1)...(x−n+1) and extract coefficients; similarly for many S(n,k) with fixed k use generating-function identity. Syntax as documented; choose algorithms suited to batch vs single queries.
